title: THE HEART THAT WOULD NOT BEND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the Israelites go." - Exodus 10:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short verse, and by now a familiar one. Pharaoh has confessed, received mercy, and refused again.

Scripture states both realities without embarrassment: Pharaoh hardened his own heart repeatedly, and God hardened Pharaoh's heart. Christians who equally honour the Bible have long differed on precisely how these fit together, and a devotional page will not settle it. What we can all affirm is that God is entirely just, that He is never the author of evil, and that Pharaoh was never an innocent man being forced into sin.

What should strike us is the sheer momentum of a hardened heart. Nine plagues. Multiple confessions. Repeated mercies. And still no change.

Hearts do not usually harden in a moment. They set gradually, like concrete — each refusal a little firmer than the last, until what was once a decision becomes a condition.

The remedy is not to wait for a bigger crisis. It is to respond to God today, while the conviction is still tender.

Scripture keeps saying it because we keep needing it: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Heb 3:15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there conviction I have been quietly setting aside?
2. What would responding to God today actually look like for me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my heart soft and responsive. Where I have been setting You aside, I turn back today. Amen.
